question: is the along-contour (tangent) error limited by local resolution or local geometry?
answer: NO -- and local sharpness makes it WORSE
mechanism: A ridge constrains position ACROSS it and says nothing about position ALONG it. Landmarks at sharp sites sit on ridges, so their along-ridge coordinate is locally unconstrained by construction. Local sharpness therefore improves the across component (already the accurate one at 0.61) and degrades the tangent component (the dominant one at 1.25).
consequence: Curvature features, per-landmark local crops and higher point density all attack local geometry, hence the across/normal components -- 23% of the error energy. They cannot address the tangent component. Expect small gains from all three.
implication: The tangent information is NON-LOCAL. Position along a ridge is fixed by where the contour STARTS and ENDS, and a ridge terminus or junction IS locally well-defined in a way that a mid-ridge point never is. That is a topological property of the ear ridge network, not a local patch property.
supporting: Per-ear errors are largely uncorrelated between contours (0.01-0.48), so there is no global failure mode. Best ear 0.544mm and best landmark 0.566mm show the pipeline reaches sub-0.6mm when the geometry allows.
